channel.title: Diffbrief · Cloud & infra
channel.description: Daily cloud & infra stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Microsoft hotpatch fixes Windows Server 2025 crashes after IPv6 route expiry
item.description: An out-of-band update addresses stop errors on some Server 2025 systems with IPv6 routes that expire after the November hotpatch. Operators using hotpatching can use the stated trigger to identify affected systems and apply the fix.

item.title: Windows Server 2028 will remove the WSUS server role
item.description: Microsoft says Windows Server 2028 will no longer include WSUS, the centralized update-management role, while earlier releases retain support. Enterprises that rely on WSUS will need to plan how they manage updates across Windows fleets.

item.title: Ubuntu 26 sudo-rs prompt breaks Ansible privilege escalation
item.description: sudo-rs prints extra text before its password prompt, confusing Ansible’s privilege-escalation detection; a fix landed in Ansible Core 2.22.0 and is being backported. This identifies a concrete automation issue for Ubuntu 26 upgrades.

item.title: NVIDIA Mission Control coordinates leak responses across liquid-cooled AI factories
item.description: Mission Control connects building-management systems, cluster managers, and BMCs, with leak policies scoped from device to building and observability through Prometheus and Grafana. AI data-center operators can use these details to assess facility automation and incident response.

item.title: Bluetooth PAN gets a Sony Ericsson S500i online after 2G shutdown
item.description: A Bluetooth Personal Area Network can carry IP traffic as Ethernet frames, letting the S500i access the internet through another device despite its lost 2G service. The workaround is a useful example of protocol-level reuse for a legacy device.

item.title: Cloudflare can mask an unencrypted IPv4 connection to an origin
item.description: The excerpt says a site can present TLS, IPv6 and post-quantum encryption to users while Cloudflare connects to its origin over unencrypted IPv4, with limited dashboard visibility. Engineers should verify the full client-to-origin path rather than relying on edge-facing indicators.

item.title: Quad9 disables DNS resolution for users in France after court demands
item.description: Quad9 says it will refuse all DNS queries from France after a court upheld demands to block domains, with fines for non-compliance. The disruption underscores how legal and provider-level changes can affect a widely used infrastructure dependency.

item.title: Kubernetes 1.38 removes kubectl WebSocket opt-out variables
item.description: Kubernetes plans to remove the environment variables that disable WebSockets for kubectl remote commands and port forwarding; WebSockets will remain the first choice with SPDY fallback. Teams should check scripts and CI environments for those variables before upgrading.

item.title: Stalwart 1.2 adds Exchange protocols for Outlook-compatible self-hosting
item.description: Stalwart 1.2 implements MAPI over HTTP, EWS, Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover, allowing common mail clients to connect for mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes. It offers organizations evaluating self-hosted mail a concrete compatibility option.

item.title: Debian splits iperf packages and adds a hardened server service
item.description: Debian’s packaging now separates iperf client and server packages, with systemd and ufw integration and a dynamically assigned service user with hardening. These operational details make a common network-testing tool easier to deploy with safer defaults.

item.title: AWS customer impact can go unnoticed when status reporting lags
item.description: The column says AWS’s status site has historically been slow to reflect customer experience and discusses what Downdetector does and does not show. Incident visibility and status communication shape how teams assess reliability.

item.title: GitHub Actions accepts YAML constructs rejected by conforming parsers
item.description: GitHub Actions accepts YAML constructs that a conforming YAML 1.2.2 parser rejects, including a flow-style value indented at the parent level. That mismatch can make workflow tooling reject definitions GitHub itself runs.

item.title: Anthropic’s 2028 power mix is projected to be 87% gas and 11% coal
item.description: The report analyzes Anthropic’s compute commitments and estimates that fossil generation will supply much of the power for AI data centers. Its estimates and underlying dataset offer context for infrastructure planning and the energy constraints on AI capacity.

item.title: A Stratum 2 NTP server joins the public pool using GNSS-backed time
item.description: A studio Stratum 2 server draws time from a GNSS-backed Stratum 1 Pi, and the author outlines practical requirements for pool operators. It offers a small-scale look at maintaining a public time service.

item.title: AWS Emulator lets Terraform tests exercise AWS API endpoints
item.description: The tool emulates AWS API endpoints to help catch cases where a successful Terraform plan still fails at apply time. Testing against API behavior can reduce infrastructure changes that only fail after deployment.

item.title: HyperPod combines GPU, network, and host diagnostics for training workloads
item.description: The observability update brings diagnostic and profiling capabilities for EKS- and Slurm-based training, pinpointing issues across GPU, network, and host layers. It targets a recurring challenge in diagnosing failures across distributed training infrastructure.

item.title: A monitor setup cut download speed from 2.4 Gbps to 600 Mbps
item.description: The author reports download speed falling to 600 Mbps while upload stayed at 2.4 Gbps after moving connections to a Studio Display XDR. The debugging story may offer useful performance-investigation lessons, though the excerpt does not reveal the cause.

item.title: PcapAnalyzer checks captures for 27 network faults
item.description: The self-hosted beta checks packet captures for TCP, routing, DNS, DHCP, application, and tunnel problems, with severity levels and next steps. It could shorten network troubleshooting without sending captures off-machine.

item.title: Windows Server 2028 defaults to hardened Server Core and adds VM protections
item.description: Windows Server 2028 adds a hardened Server Core default, a security baseline, Trusted Launch for VM boot integrity, and initial Confidential VM support. The changes matter to teams setting secure defaults and protecting server fleets.

item.title: GKE ambient networking brings a sidecarless service mesh to GA
item.description: Ambient networking moves mesh responsibilities from application pods to shared per-node components and managed control-plane services. Teams running service meshes can weigh the resource and operational trade-offs of a sidecarless design.

item.title: GKE previews in-place migration to its eBPF-based Dataplane V2
item.description: The preview lets eligible VPC-native clusters migrate from Dataplane V1 to the eBPF- and Cilium-based V2 without first creating a parallel cluster. This addresses a real migration constraint for stateful workloads and established IP allocations.

item.title: GKE previews IPv6-only nodes and pods for AI and ML workloads
item.description: GKE’s preview runs nodes and pods without private IPv4 on Cloud TPU v6e and CPU pools, using DNS64/NAT64 to reach IPv4 endpoints. This gives large AI deployments another option when private IPv4 address space is exhausted.

item.title: Orchestrated pytest workers run 58,000 integration tests in about 2.5 minutes
item.description: Close says its backend CI runs nearly 58,000 integration tests, many hitting datastores, in about two and a half minutes using orchestrated pytest workers. The write-up offers a performance case study for teams with slow integration-test pipelines.

item.title: DNS resolvers are a poor enforcement point for blocking piracy
item.description: Quad9 says it will stop answering DNS queries from France after a court fined it for refusing to block pirate sports-streaming domains. The dispute highlights how legal demands can affect the availability and policies of shared network infrastructure.

item.title: Quad9 withdraws its French DNS resolver after a court-ordered blocking ruling
item.description: Quad9 says it will leave France rather than comply with court-ordered domain blocking and daily financial penalties. The case shows how legal demands can force changes to the operation and availability of public DNS infrastructure.

item.title: Slurm HRES schedules QPUs as cluster-level resources
item.description: Slurm 26.11 HRES plugins associate QPUs with eligible nodes and handle health checks, admission, and release without reserving compute nodes while waiting. The pattern shows how schedulers can model specialized resources cleanly.

item.title: Orbital data centers face questions about cost, cooling and scaling
item.description: The report examines orbital data-center economics, launch timelines, thermal management, radiation, bandwidth and security, with appendices on degradation and cost assumptions. Its analysis bears on the infrastructure and operating constraints behind proposed AI capacity.

item.title: Intercept HTTP/3 by relaying QUIC and decoding QPACK streams
item.description: The guide explains why TCP-based HTTP proxies miss HTTP/3, then walks through intercepting QUIC traffic and handling QPACK's dynamic table in browsers. It gives engineers a practical path to inspect and replay traffic when debugging modern web protocols.

item.title: Kubernetes plans to remove kube-proxy’s IPVS backend in 1.40
item.description: Kubernetes plans to remove IPVS because it is complex to maintain and cannot correctly implement every Kubernetes Service edge case; users should migrate to nftables or iptables. The rationale and migration options matter to teams operating Kubernetes networking.

item.title: 400 US hyperscale data centers used as much electricity as Michigan
item.description: A Harvard study reported that 400 US hyperscale data centers used as much electricity as Michigan in a year, with emissions three times higher than before the AI boom. Power demand is an important constraint on scaling AI infrastructure.

item.title: Eclipse Mosquitto provides an MQTT broker and client utilities
item.description: Mosquitto implements MQTT 5.0, 3.1.1 and 3.1, with C and C++ client libraries and command-line publishing, subscribing and administration tools. It is a useful building block for systems that exchange messages over a standard protocol.

item.title: Unlimited customer namespaces led S2 to consider running authoritative DNS
item.description: S2 needed unlimited basin subdomains, each routed by CNAME, with strong consistency so new addresses would not be blocked by cached NXDOMAIN responses. The case illustrates the operational tradeoffs behind replacing a managed DNS service.

item.title: A local pkgbase mirror avoids repeated FreeBSD package downloads across jails
item.description: Converting FreeBSD jails to pkgbase caused the author’s setup to fetch packages from official mirrors 36 times; the guide shows how to mirror them locally with Apache. Operators deploying many systems can apply the bandwidth-saving approach.

item.title: Tor 0.4.9.17 adds IPv6 relay DoS defenses during an ongoing attack
item.description: Tor's rapid-response release includes an IPv6-related relay DoS defense as an attack overwhelms most relays. Operators of distributed services can learn from how the project is responding to a network-wide availability threat.

item.title: Kiri reports 22 ms container startup versus 178 ms for Docker Desktop
item.description: Kiri says `docker run` takes 22 ms versus 178 ms on Docker Desktop, measured on 2 CPUs and 8 GB. The comparison is useful for local container workflows, though it covers startup time rather than broader performance.

item.title: tsoracle combines strictly increasing timestamps with gapless sequences
item.description: The Rust service issues ordered timestamps and contiguous sequences using one round-trip and a durable counter per named key, with no gaps across crashes or failover. That combination targets distributed databases, audit logs and systems that need gapless identifiers, though the excerpt provides no performance evidence.

item.title: Nix’s eval-profiler samples evaluator stacks for flamegraph analysis
item.description: Nix can sample its function-call stack during evaluation and emit profiles for `flamegraph.pl`, with configurable frequency and output path. Engineers diagnosing slow Nix evaluations can turn the profile into a visual call-site breakdown.

item.title: Google Cloud previews Lumen-powered last-mile Cross-Cloud Interconnect
item.description: The preview extends Google Cloud’s managed interconnect service to private clouds, data centers, neoclouds, and other clouds. Teams running workloads and AI pipelines across environments may benefit from simpler high-bandwidth connectivity.

item.title: Lonewolf 0.3 adds federation to its standalone XMPP server
item.description: The Rust server can now exchange messages, presence, and subscriptions with other XMPP servers; federation is enabled by default when a host has a certificate and public DNS name. The release is a useful concrete update on operating a small federated service.

item.title: A copper-wire upgrade triggered the nationwide US flight ground stop
item.description: The transport secretary said an issue during a copper-to-fibre upgrade caused a router to flood other air-traffic-control systems; officials had not ruled out equipment or contractor error. The incident highlights the operational risk of modernizing old critical infrastructure.
